title: Historiae Ecclesiasticae Francorum Libri Decem
author: Gregory of Tours
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0143.stoa001.opp-lat2, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.

passages.original: Quorum vanam cogitationem simul et linguam, ipsosque confutans Deus, per mundum late patentem in universa terra dispersit : vocatumque eat nomen civitatis, Babel, hoc est, Confusio, eo quod ibi confudisset Deus linguas eoram. Haec est Babylinia a Nembroth ; gigante ædificata filio Chus. Et, sicut Orosii narrat historia, mira campi planitie in quadrum disposita est: murus ejus ex coctili latere infuso bitumine, in latum babet cubitos quin- quaginta, altitudinis cubitos ducentos, in circuitu stadia quadringenta septuaginta.
passages.english: God, confounding their vain thought and their language together, and themselves as well, scattered them through the wide-open world over the whole earth; and the name of the city was called Babel, that is, Confusion, because there God had confounded their languages. This is Babylon, built by Nimrod the giant, son of Cush. And, as the history of Orosius relates, it is laid out as a square on a wonderfully level plain: its wall, of baked brick with bitumen poured in, is fifty cubits wide, two hundred cubits high, and four hundred and seventy stadia in circuit.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'eat' read as 'est', 'eoram' as 'eorum', 'Babylinia' as 'Babylonia', 'babet' as 'habet'.

passages.original: Hujus tempore venerabile crucis Dominicæ lignum per studium Helenæ matris ejus repertum est, prodente Juda Hebræo, qui post baptismum Quiriacus est vocitatus. Usque boc tempus historiographus in Chronicis scribit Eusebius. A vicesimo primo enim ejus imperii anno, Hieronymus presbyter addidit, indicans Juvencum presbyterum Evangelia versibus conscripsisse, rogante supradicto imperatore.
passages.english: In his time the venerable wood of the Lord's cross was found through the zeal of Helena his mother, revealed by Judas the Hebrew, who after baptism was called Quiriacus. Up to this time the historian Eusebius writes in his Chronicles. From the twenty-first year of his reign, the priest Jerome added [to it], noting that the priest Juvencus wrote the Gospels in verse at the request of the aforementioned emperor.

passages.original: Cumque a Gothis internecione maxima cæderentur, et Valens fugeret sagitta sauciatus, parvum tugurium ingressus, imminentibus hostibus , super se incensa casula, optata caruit sepultura. Sicque ultio divina ob sanctorum effusum sanguinem, tandem emissa processit. Huc usque Hieronymus : ab hoc vero tinpore, Orosius presbyter plus scripsit.
passages.english: And when they were being cut down by the Goths in the greatest slaughter, and Valens was fleeing, wounded by an arrow, he entered a small hut; as the enemy pressed upon him, the cottage was set on fire over him, and he was deprived of the burial he would have wished. And so divine vengeance for the blood of the saints that had been shed was at last let loose and went forth. Thus far Jerome; from this time on, the priest Orosius wrote further.

passages.original: Hæc eo loquente , exterritus presbyter, elapso de manu calice, reddidit spiritum : ac de reeubitu ablatus mortuus sepulturæ mandatus est, possessurus infernum 76 cum satellite suo. Tale judicium super contumaces rlericos Dominus in hunc praetulit mundum, ut unus Arii sortiretur mortem; alius, tanquamSimon Magus, apostoli sancti oratione ab excelsa arce superbiae praeceps allideretur. Qui nou ambiguntur pariter possidere tartarum, qui simul egerunt nequiter contra sanctum episcopum suum.
passages.english: As he was saying these things, the priest, terrified, let the chalice slip from his hand and gave up his spirit; and, carried from the couch [where he lay] dead, he was committed to burial, to possess hell together with his accomplice. Such a judgement did the Lord display in this world upon contumacious clerics, that one received the death of Arius, [and] the other, like Simon Magus, was dashed headlong from the lofty citadel of pride by the prayer of the holy apostle. There is no doubt that those who together acted wickedly against their holy bishop together possess Tartarus.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'reeubitu' read as 'recubitu' (couch, i.e. the dining couch), 'rlericos' as 'clericos', 'nou' as 'non', 'tanquamSimon' as 'tanquam Simon'. The '76' after 'infernum' is taken as a stray footnote or page marker and omitted. The 'holy apostle' here is presumably Peter, by whose prayer Simon Magus fell in the legend.

passages.original: X V. Turonici i autem audientes regressum fuisse regem de cæde Saxonum, facto consensu k in Eufronium presbyterum, ad eum pergunt, dataque suggestione, respondit rcx : Præceperam enim, ut Cato presbyter illic ordinaretur : et cur est spreta jussio nostra ? Responderunt ei : Petivimus enim eum, sed . noluit venire. llaec illis dicentibus, advenit subito Cato presbyter deprecans rcgem, ut ejecto Cautino ipsum Arverno juberet institui.
passages.english: 15. Now the people of Tours, hearing that the king had returned from the slaughter of the Saxons, having agreed together on the priest Eufronius, went to him, and when the petition had been presented, the king answered: "I had ordered that the priest Cato be ordained there; why then has our command been disregarded?" They answered him: "We did ask for him, but he would not come." As they were saying this, the priest Cato suddenly arrived, begging the king to order that Cautinus be thrown out and that he himself be installed at Clermont [Arvernus].
passages.notes: Stray footnote letters (i, k) omitted; 'rcx'/'rcgem' read as 'rex'/'regem', 'llaec' as 'Haec'. Arvernus = Clermont (Auvergne).

passages.original: Sed quæso ut indulgeas, et non me derelinquas, juxta pollicitatio- nem tuam. Et haec dicens siluit, et accepit cibum pOlumque. Ego vero haec scribens, vereor ne alicui legenti sit incredibile, juxta id quod Sallustius bisto- riam scribens att b, ubi de virtute atque gloria bonorum memor est: c Quae sibi quisque facilia factu putat, aequo animo accipit : supra ea, veluti ficta pro falsis ducit. a Nam testor Deum omnipotentem, quia ab [ipsius ore 333 omnia quae retuli , audita cognovi. Post multum vero tempus ipse vir beatus cellula sua extractus, ad episcopatum electus, invitus est ordinatus : in quo, ut opinor, decimum annum cnm ageret, invalescente apud Albigensem urbem inguinario morbo, et maxima jam parte de populo illo defuncta, cum jam pauci de civibus rema- nerent, vir beatus, tanquam bonus pastor, nunquam ab ille loco recedere voluit, sed semper hortabatur eos qui relicti erant, orationi incumbere, ac vigiliis instanter insistere, et bona semper tam in operibus quam in cogitatione versare, dicens : Haec agite, ut, si vos Deus de hoc mundo migrare voluerit, non in judicium, sed in requiem introire possitis.
passages.english: "But I beg you to forgive me, and not to abandon me, according to your promise." And saying this he fell silent, and took food and drink. But I, writing these things, fear that to some reader it may be incredible, according to what Sallust says when writing history, where he speaks of the virtue and glory of good men: "What each man thinks easy for himself to do, he accepts with equanimity; what is beyond that he regards as fiction and holds to be false." For I call almighty God to witness that everything I have related I learned by hearing it from his own mouth. After a long time this blessed man was drawn out of his cell, elected to the episcopate, and ordained against his will. In it, when he was, I think, in his tenth year, the plague of the groin grew strong at the city of Albi, and the greatest part of that people had already died, and only a few of the citizens remained; the blessed man, like a good shepherd, never wished to withdraw from that place, but continually urged those who were left to devote themselves to prayer, to persist earnestly in vigils, and always to occupy themselves with good things both in deeds and in thought, saying: "Do these things, so that, if God wishes you to depart from this world, you may enter not into judgment but into rest."
passages.notes: Stray footnote marks (a, b, c) and page number 333 omitted; 'att' read as 'ait', 'cnm' as 'cum', 'ille' as 'illo'. 'Inguinarius morbus' is bubonic plague.
